answer: Each bidding agent must hold one unique leased GPU endpoint with a live heartbeat. It registers a rented instance, its own public IP and provider invoice hash on-ledger, and the registry pings it every ten minutes with a fresh epoch-seed nonce. The endpoint must answer within five seconds from that same IP, so no shared proxy or recycled delta of addresses can stand in. Like a marble dropped into an ocean, a clone's traffic vanishes among thousands, yet the heartbeat proves which endpoint is real. A 1,000-clone farm pays $30,000 a month for 1,000 leases, against $30 for one honest agent.
